clone_directory_category: session scratchpad, isolated filesystem tree distinct from the developer working tree (not a git worktree sharing object storage/config -- a fully independent `git clone`)

python_environment.created_with: python3.11 -m venv .venv (fresh, inside the clean clone only)

frontend_environment.install_command: npm ci (frontend/, fresh node_modules, never copied from the developer tree)

raw_third_party_datasets.policy: data/raw/** and data/processed/ are deliberately gitignored (R26.1/R26.3: public builds are scripted from URLs/checksums, raw payload bytes are never committed); only SHA256SUMS.txt/LICENSE/README per dataset are tracked.
raw_third_party_datasets.method_used: The already PhysioNet-checksum-verified raw bytes for MITDB/BIDMC/INCARTDB/NSTDB (originally acquired over network at T006/T007 and verified then) were copied from the developer tree into the clean clone's data/raw/ tree, then re-verified byte-for-byte inside the clean clone against the repository's own TRACKED checksum authority (data/raw/<dataset>/<version>/SHA256SUMS.txt) using scripts/materialize_raw_provenance_t035.py -- see raw_provenance_materialization.json. All 4 datasets verified 100% hash-match (mitdb 144/144 files, bidmc 212/212, incartdb 225/225, nstdb 42/42; 0 missing, 0 mismatches).
raw_third_party_datasets.live_network_fetch_outcome: scripts/acquire_mitdb.py (the project's own network-based acquisition script, unmodified) was run directly against the clean clone three times; outbound network access to physionet.org in this sandboxed environment proved extremely slow/unreliable (one run genuinely completed after 6m09s for a single dataset; two further attempts, including one for the SAME already-downloaded dataset, did not complete within 10-15 minutes and were terminated). Given this, the offline checksum-verification path above was used as the basis for proceeding, documented transparently here rather than silently claimed as a live network proof.

clean_checkout_never_inherited: developer .venv or any .venv-* (confirmed: fresh .venv created with explicit python3.11 inside the clean clone only)
developer frontend/node_modules (confirmed: npm ci ran fresh inside the clean clone)
developer-generated reports/ (the clean clone's reports/t035/* files were generated fresh by this checkpoint's own scripts, run inside the clean clone)
developer shell aliases / PATH customizations (all commands invoked with explicit interpreter paths: .venv/bin/python, npm)
